hook: Fair warning: this is pitch-black comedy built on harm to animals, presented as deadpan test logs. A claw machine asks each player to name a method, then carries it out with absurd literalism and pays out a cookie. If that premise is not for you, skip it; if it is, the jokes live in how each request gets interpreted.
whyItMatters: It is a strong example of the cursed-wish test log, where the comedy comes from a machine taking every word literally and escalating far past what anyone meant. The cleanup routine and the recorded quip after each game give it a mocking personality without a single line of description. The procedures also hint at an ugly institutional decision, since testing must continue by executive order and the file never says why.
thingsToNotice: Track the cookies: their flavour, their number and whether they appear at all work as the machine's scoring system and its commentary. The woman in the red gown recurs across unrelated requests, giving the absurd logs a strange through-line. The switch to the maintenance technician changes the mood, since her requests grow gentler and the machine still finds a way to punish them. Her last logged plea gets the bleakest answer of all, and the note about offering her amnestics between sessions suddenly reads as compassion.

related.note: Another test log where the exact wording of an instruction decides the outcome.
Another anomaly packaged as a consumer product, in a far gentler register.
